title: Choose the broadside composition
question: All three use the same approved woodland-broadside world. Choose the hierarchy that should govern the finished page.

options.label: Courier overlap
options.thesis: The letter ritual leads, with the terminal proof tucked into the same physical scene.
options.viewport: A monumental promise, squirrel courier, branch, and terminal proof overlap as one authored printed sheet.
options.risk: The overlap requires careful responsive translation so the evidence never competes with the sentence.

options.label: Editorial split
options.thesis: The emotional promise and the working release sit side by side with equal confidence.
options.viewport: A huge left-hand promise faces one solid download-and-terminal field on the right, with the next chapter visible below.
options.risk: The right field must not become a conventional product card.

options.label: Quiet proclamation
options.thesis: One unforgettable sentence owns the screen, followed immediately by download and proof.
options.viewport: The centered promise fills the upper half; one moss action and a wide terminal strip anchor the lower half.
options.risk: It can become poster-like unless the proof and following content remain clearly interactive web structure.

outcome: Superseded by direct user feedback. None of these broadside compositions ships; the final page uses the simpler folded-letter reference and keeps the courier clear of all text and controls.
